messages:
cheng: heads up — zephyr-v3q int8 canary is spiking funcall parse failures, ~4.3% on the sample set. observed patterns: trailing commas, lone string payloads, and occasional NDJSON fragments. logs attached below.

lia: ack. can you paste a small example of the raw model output we failed to parse? are these coming from streaming responses or non-streamed?

cheng: streaming. here's a normalized excerpt (sanitized):
```
{"action":"lookup","args": {"id": 42,}}

"{"action":"noop"}

{"results": [1,2,3]
```
first and last have trailing commas / missing closing brace; middle one is a quoted JSON string.

alex: these look like two failure classes: (1) mild truncation/commas from tokenizer boundary, (2) model wrapping JSON in a string. For (2) we can add a lightweight unquote+reparse pass before calling the strict schema validator.

rafa: telemetry note — failures correlate with prompt templates that include long JSON prefixes (user history + tools list). risk goes up when sequence length > 600. also saw that kv-cache prefixing pushes the model to emit extra commas near the end.

cheng: proposal: for canary rollout, enable a "lenient-parsing" stage with heuristics: 1) strip leading/trailing quotes and unescape, 2) remove trailing commas in objects/arrays, 3) try NDJSON split if top-level parse fails. we already have these heuristics in local eval harness — want to test in canary only.

lia: fine, but add metrics so we can compare: raw_parse_fail_rate, lenient_recover_rate, strict_accept_rate, and downstream-tool-error-rate. also we need to be careful not to hide real semantic errors by aggressive heuristics.

alex: agreed. here's the quick config I propose for the canary parser hook (pseudo):
```yaml
parser_hooks:
  - name: unquote-reparse
    enabled: true
  - name: trailing-comma-strip
    enabled: true
  - name: ndjson-split
    enabled: true
    max_lines: 5
  - metrics: [raw_parse_fail, lenient_success, strict_success, tool_errors]
  - sample_rate: 0.05  # 5% of canary traffic for now
```

rafa: also add a safety gate: if lenient_success / raw_parse_fail < 0.2 (i.e., heuristics recover very rarely) then auto-disable heuristics and alert. keeps us from masking a deeper model regression.

canary-bot: deploy-canary: zephyr-v3q-int8 parser-hook=true sample_rate=0.05 initiated by cheng at 2026-02-18T15:12:12Z :rocket:

cheng: running the canary now. I'll attach a small repro script for the eval harness so others can run offline. key logs I'll watch: parse_fail_histogram, token_positions_of_first_parse_error, and post-tool-error-rate.

lia: please tag me when you have the metric dashboard link. if lenient parsing recovers > 80% and downstream tool errors don't increase, we can promote heuristics into the default onboarding pipeline for int8. otherwise revert and open a model regression ticket.

alex: one more idea — add a tiny postprocess prompt to nudge outputs toward canonical JSON: append \n\nPlease respond only with valid JSON matching the schema. as a last-turn suffix for the canary and measure effect. cheap experiment.

cheng: good call. I'll run both variants in parallel: 50% with parser hooks, 50% with postprocess prompt, sample_rate still 5%. will report numbers in ~2h.

rafa: thanks. if this looks noisy we should also snapshot the tokenized output around the failure boundary so runtime kernel selection folks can inspect whether quantization is introducing tokenization artifacts.

cheng: noted. saving token window +/- 8 tokens around parse boundary. will post results. :mag:
